title: Residual factor pairs
connection: Fixing x turns 4/p−1/x=a/b into (ay−b)(az−b)=b²; connect ES to complementary divisors in simultaneous residue classes.
why: This is an exact two-unit-fraction reformulation rather than a counting analogy.
first_step: For primes below 500, enumerate x up to p and record the successful residue pairs.

title: Moving the first denominator
connection: Connect changes x→x+1 with changes in the residual factor-pair problem, treating consecutive x as coupled rather than independent trials.
why: Neighboring residual numerators differ by four, so their divisor searches share arithmetic structure.
first_step: Tabulate success transitions between neighboring x for 100 primes.

title: Denominator gcd stratification
connection: Partition ES triples by the three pairwise denominator gcds and compare the strata with multiplicative parametrizations.
why: The cleared equation 4xyz=p(xy+xz+yz) imposes exact constraints on every gcd stratum.
first_step: Derive the cleared equation after writing x=ga and y=gb with gcd(a,b)=1.

title: Primitive projective triples
connection: View denominator triples as rational points up to common scaling, with p recovered from their reciprocal sum.
why: Scaling explains why prime cases are central and may separate shape from arithmetic size.
first_step: Enumerate primitive triples with coordinates below 100 and sort the resulting reduced values of 4xyz/(xy+xz+yz).

title: Symmetric coordinates
connection: Use s1=x+y+z, s2=xy+xz+yz, s3=xyz and the relation 4s3=ps2 to connect ES to integer-root cubic polynomials.
why: The cubic viewpoint keeps all denominator permutations together and exposes discriminant constraints.
first_step: Search small integer s1,s2 satisfying integral roots of T³−s1T²+s2T−ps2/4.

title: Discriminant squares
connection: After fixing one symmetric parameter, require the remaining quadratic discriminant to be square; compare with Pell-type searches.
why: Square conditions can package an infinite family more economically than individual divisors.
first_step: Derive the discriminant after prescribing y+z and x, then identify when a Pell equation appears.

title: Near-equal denominator perturbations
connection: Write y=z+h and study the exact residual equation as h varies, connecting ES to near-square factorization.
why: Small h gives structured, checkable subfamilies without claiming they cover every prime.
first_step: Enumerate the smallest attainable difference z−y for primes below 1000.

title: Denominator ratios as slopes
connection: Parameterize y/z by a reduced rational slope and express the ES condition in terms of its numerator and denominator.
why: A rational slope organizes triples differently from fixing x and might reveal short covering families.
first_step: Derive the divisibility condition for y=ku,z=kv with gcd(u,v)=1.

title: Fraction splitting trees
connection: Connect ES identities to the elementary split 1/a=1/(a+1)+1/(a(a+1)), allowing merges as well as splits.
why: Length-three targets might be reached through longer identities with controlled cancellation or merging.
first_step: Generate a bounded graph of positive unit-fraction identities connected by exact splits and inverse merges.

title: Weighted mediants
connection: Compare residual fractions from neighboring x with Farey mediants, looking for intervals where a two-term decomposition persists.
why: Farey adjacency controls numerator-denominator determinants exactly.
first_step: Compute Farey neighbors of residual fractions for the first 50 difficult primes.

title: Bilinear determinant encoding
connection: Represent uv−r as a two-by-two determinant and translate ES divisor conditions into determinant equations with congruences.
why: Determinants bring row operations and lattice bases into a directly arithmetic setting.
first_step: Write a residual factor-pair certificate as a determinant condition and list congruence-preserving row operations.

title: Cluster-style mutations
connection: Search for involutions on auxiliary ES parametrizations analogous to replacing one root of a quadratic while fixing other variables.
why: An exact positive integral mutation could propagate certificates across a connected graph.
first_step: For three existing elementary parametrizations, solve for each coordinate and test whether another integral branch exists.

title: Vieta moves on lifted equations
connection: Introduce an auxiliary variable making an ES constraint quadratic, then examine Vieta root exchange.
why: Lifting may create useful symmetries absent from the original equation, but integrality must be checked.
first_step: Try y+z=s and yz=q, derive the lifted equations, and test root-exchange closures.

title: Resultants between identities
connection: Eliminate shared parameters from two valid ES families to identify their intersections and potential transition rules.
why: Intersections may show how families cooperate rather than merely duplicate coverage.
first_step: Compute a resultant for two small exact families found by direct denominator ansatz.

title: Saturation and boundary components
connection: Study the ideal of 4xyz−p(xy+xz+yz) after excluding zero coordinates and compare its components under congruence restrictions.
why: Removing degenerate solutions is essential before algebraic parametrizations are interpreted arithmetically.
first_step: Compute the saturation by xyz for a small symbolic specialization and inspect the nonzero locus.

title: Birational chart comparison
connection: Cover the ES surface by different rational charts and compare where integer points have manageable denominators.
why: One chart can hide integrality that another makes explicit.
first_step: Write charts obtained by solving for x, y, and a denominator ratio; compare their divisibility conditions.

title: Height functions on certificates
connection: Compare max(x,y,z), xyz, and auxiliary-parameter height as costs on the same certificate space.
why: A proof-producing descent may work for a height unrelated to the smallest denominator.
first_step: For bounded triples, build move graphs and test which heights decrease along known identity transformations.

title: Logarithmic denominator coordinates
connection: Map triples to log(x),log(y),log(z), comparing thin certificate families with the curved positive ES surface.
why: Multiplicative scales become additive and can expose regions systematically missed by bounded boxes.
first_step: Plot normalized log-denominator triples for primes below 1000 using several search cutoffs.

title: Tropical balance regimes
connection: Separate the cleared equation into regimes according to which of xy,xz,yz dominate, using tropical-style bookkeeping.
why: Dominant balances may suggest complementary denominator ansatzes, not replace exact arithmetic.
first_step: List possible valuation balances at a prime dividing one denominator and derive the corresponding exact divisibility cases.

title: Newton polytope viewpoints
connection: Compare monomial supports of the ES surface and auxiliary divisor equations to find sparse elimination orders.
why: Sparse structure can reduce symbolic-search complexity without implying integer-point existence.
first_step: Draw the exponent support and test elimination with two variable orders in a computer algebra system.

title: Pell families from denominator gaps
connection: Prescribe an affine relation between two denominators and ask when the resulting square condition yields a Pell family.
why: An infinite family of certificates could arise from a recurrent rather than polynomial parametrization.
first_step: Test y=z−h with h in 1 through 20 and classify the resulting discriminant equations.

title: Elliptic slices
connection: Intersect the ES surface with simple quadratic constraints and check whether the resulting curves have genus one.
why: A useful slice could carry arithmetic group operations, although positivity and integrality remain separate tasks.
first_step: Try xy=z²+k for small k and compute the genus of the resulting plane curve.

title: Conic bundles
connection: Choose auxiliary coordinates that leave a conic equation over one parameter and study its local solvability and integral points.
why: Conics admit explicit parametrizations once a rational point is supplied.
first_step: Search linear substitutions that make one residual equation quadratic in two remaining variables.

title: Norm equations
connection: Rewrite selected quadratic discriminant conditions as norms in quadratic orders and track the congruences needed for ES.
why: Multiplicativity of norms may combine certificates in ways raw divisor enumeration misses.
first_step: For one Pell-type slice, translate the equation into a norm and record its positivity restrictions.

title: Class-group bookkeeping
connection: When a divisor condition factors in a quadratic order, distinguish principal from nonprincipal ideal factors.
why: This identifies an arithmetic constraint that could guide which auxiliary field is useful.
first_step: For a small negative discriminant arising from a slice, compare ideal factorizations with actual integral certificates.

title: Gaussian integer decompositions
connection: Test whether representing auxiliary factors as sums of two squares helps impose the needed residue class.
why: Norm factors carry extra structure; the connection is a candidate construction, not a universal representation claim.
first_step: For small certificates with a sum-of-two-squares auxiliary factor, tabulate how Gaussian factors determine residues.

title: Quaternion multiplication as composition
connection: Ask whether quaternion norm identities compose two partial ES certificates into a full one.
why: Four-square identities offer explicit polynomial relations whose congruences can be checked.
first_step: Choose a small norm identity and symbolically test whether its cross terms match an ES residual equation.

title: Trace identities in SL₂
connection: Connect two-by-two matrix trace identities with the campaign's word formulations and seek trace-preserving congruence moves.
why: Matrix words package nonlinear integer expressions into exact multiplication laws.
first_step: Derive the trace relation for three short elementary matrices and compare it with tuv−u−v.

title: Continued-fraction surgery
connection: Study local replacements in continued fractions that change a certificate's congruence data without making its length too large.
why: Equivalent rational expansions can trade coefficient signs, sizes, and parity.
first_step: Enumerate short continued-fraction identities and label which preserve positivity and desired coefficient classes.

title: Continuants modulo powers of two
connection: Analyze short continuant recurrences modulo 8,16,32 and compare reachable states with the admissible coordinate classes.
why: Finite parity information may guide an otherwise unbounded integer construction.
first_step: Build the exact transition graph for continuants modulo 16 with coefficient residues as labels.

title: Stern–Brocot ancestry
connection: Attach each residual rational to its Stern–Brocot path and look for common terminal patterns among successful splits.
why: Path suffixes may encode useful divisibility conditions more compactly than numerator-denominator pairs.
first_step: Record path suffixes of length at most eight for successful and unsuccessful bounded residual searches.

title: Euclidean quotient parity
connection: Track parity of Euclidean quotients together with remainder size when processing p and an auxiliary parameter.
why: Parity-decorated Euclidean descent could interact with the required classes modulo four.
first_step: Compute quotient-parity strings for certificates found by a fixed divisor search and compare with controls.

title: Reciprocity as a design constraint
connection: Rather than discard square-like obstructions, use quadratic reciprocity to choose parameters with deliberately opposite symbols.
why: Symbols can guide which certificate family is worth trying at each prime.
first_step: For a small family, derive the Legendre-symbol necessary conditions and search complementary parameter choices.

title: Higher power residue labels
connection: Decorate auxiliary divisors with cubic or quartic residue data to distinguish classes invisible to quadratic symbols.
why: Extra labels might reveal a constructive partition even when they do not force existence.
first_step: For primes in suitable congruence classes, compare certificate frequencies across power-residue labels.

title: p-adic denominator balance
connection: Classify valuations of x,y,z at p using the cleared equation and compare branches of the classification.
why: The valuation constraints are exact and can reduce redundancy in parametrizations.
first_step: Derive all possible minimum-valuation patterns before searching examples for each pattern.

title: Hensel lifting with size control
connection: Lift auxiliary congruence solutions modulo prime powers while tracking whether representatives stay inside useful positive intervals.
why: Local lifting is only a component, but controlled representatives could feed a global construction.
first_step: Lift one divisor-family congruence from modulus q to q² and measure least positive representatives.

title: Chinese remainder optimization
connection: Treat parameter selection as a CRT problem with a cost function on the resulting least positive representative.
why: Congruence compatibility and parameter size are distinct, computable parts of certificate design.
first_step: Combine three small valid congruence conditions and optimize the CRT representative by varying their residues.

title: Rational reconstruction
connection: Use modular solutions plus height bounds to reconstruct candidate rational parametrizations of ES certificates.
why: Rational reconstruction is an exact computational tool when the bounds are justified.
first_step: For a fixed prime, reconstruct small ratios y/z from modular solutions at successively larger moduli.

title: Lattice basis reduction for residues
connection: Encode simultaneous divisibility and smallness conditions as an integer lattice and use reduced bases to propose auxiliary parameters.
why: Short vectors can suggest candidates even without an existence theorem.
first_step: Build a two-constraint lattice for one residual factor search and compare reduced vectors with brute force.

title: Geometry of numbers in moving boxes
connection: Study certificate lattices with anisotropic boxes adapted to denominator size rather than symmetric balls.
why: The natural coordinates can have very different scales, affecting any useful volume estimate.
first_step: For a fixed auxiliary modulus, derive the lattice determinant and plot the feasible box as p varies.

title: Fundamental domain boundary crossings
connection: Follow a moving residue target through lattice fundamental domains as p changes and record when short representatives appear.
why: Boundary crossings may explain abrupt changes in the cheapest certificate.
first_step: Track nearest lattice representatives for consecutive admissible primes in one explicit two-variable model.

title: Semigroup holes
connection: Treat attainable certificate parameters under positive identity composition as an affine semigroup and inspect its holes.
why: Eventual saturation is a meaningful possibility even when small exceptions persist.
first_step: Generate the semigroup from a small set of verified composition moves and compute missing points in a bounded region.

title: Frobenius coin analogies
connection: Compare admissible sums of auxiliary parameters with numerical semigroup conductor problems.
why: If a certificate construction is additive in one coordinate, conductor bounds could convert families into eventual coverage.
first_step: Find an exact ansatz with an additive free coordinate before computing its attainable residues and gaps.

title: Divisor posets
connection: Organize divisors of each p-tied integer by divisibility and study where the target residue first occurs.
why: Poset structure may reveal that a few prime-factor toggles suffice to reach the target.
first_step: Construct divisor Hasse diagrams for 20 auxiliary integers and color nodes by target residues.

title: Subset products in residue groups
connection: Translate selection of a divisor into selecting prime-power factors whose product hits a residue in a finite multiplicative group.
why: This gives an exact finite combinatorial problem once the factorization is known.
first_step: For a factored auxiliary integer, run subset-product dynamic programming and inspect unreachable residue classes.

title: Zero-sum theory for divisor residues
connection: Take discrete-log coordinates when available and compare target divisor residues with zero-sum sequence phenomena.
why: Multiplicative divisor selection becomes additive combinatorics in finite abelian groups.
first_step: For cyclic unit groups of small moduli, compute the exponent multiset and shortest subsequences hitting the target.

title: Nonunit residue handling
connection: Separate auxiliary prime factors sharing the modulus from unit factors before applying group-based divisor heuristics.
why: Ignoring nonunits would make the group model false; stratifying valuations repairs it.
first_step: Implement a residue-state enumeration that tracks gcd with the modulus and compare it with unit-only counts.

title: Complement involutions on divisors
connection: Use d↔N/d as an involution on candidate residues and look for forced pairs or fixed points.
why: The involution is exact and may reduce search or create parity constraints on failures.
first_step: For each residue r modulo a small modulus, calculate how complementary divisors transform r when it is invertible.

title: Cyclotomic factor opportunities
connection: Choose auxiliary parameters making a p-tied expression resemble a cyclotomic value with structured factors.
why: Algebraic factorization can manufacture divisors, although the required residue must still be checked.
first_step: Search low-degree substitutions yielding a difference of squares or a cyclotomic factorization in the residual equation.

title: Composition of partial certificates
connection: Define a partial certificate as satisfying the equation and some integrality conditions, then seek operations that complete missing conditions.
why: Separating algebraic validity from integrality may make complementary constructions visible.
first_step: Create a table of rational identities with their exact integrality requirements and test pairwise compatible substitutions.

title: Divisor switching with a moving modulus
connection: Exchange the roles of a target divisor and its complementary factor in the p-tied divisor count.
why: The same certificate can be counted in two ranges, potentially exposing different analytic structure.
first_step: Write both exact summation orders for divisors d≡−1 modulo 4C of 4Cp+1.

title: Hyperbola decomposition of certificates
connection: Split divisor searches at the square root and treat small divisors and small complementary factors separately.
why: This avoids assuming every successful certificate lies in one convenient size range.
first_step: Derive a nonoverlapping hyperbola decomposition for one explicit certificate count.

title: Character orthogonality for the target class
connection: Express the target residue indicator using Dirichlet characters when the divisor is coprime to the modulus.
why: An exact character expansion separates the principal contribution from signed fluctuations.
first_step: Expand the divisor-class count for modulus 12 and compare numerically with direct enumeration.

title: Cancellation across auxiliary parameters
connection: Sum character errors over C before taking absolute values, looking for cancellation lost in parameterwise bounds.
why: Different certificate lines may compensate each other's arithmetic biases.
first_step: Compute signed nonprincipal-character contributions for C≤30 over a sample of primes.

title: A large-sieve formulation
connection: Ask whether the family of changing moduli and p-tied integers can be organized into a large-sieve-shaped quadratic form.
why: A shared quadratic form could control many residue searches simultaneously.
first_step: Write the exact matrix of character evaluations for bounded C and p, then check which large sieve formulations match it.

title: Dispersion between certificate families
connection: Compare cross-correlations of counts from two distinct auxiliary-parameter ranges rather than their separate means.
why: Mixed counts can measure whether two families fail together.
first_step: Derive the two-family second-moment expansion and isolate its diagonal terms.

title: Bilinear factor ranges
connection: Group auxiliary factorizations into dyadic boxes and inspect whether a bilinear sum emerges.
why: Bilinear structure gives more options than treating each divisor independently.
first_step: For one certificate equation, write the sum over two factor variables restricted to dyadic intervals.

title: Kloosterman-shaped inverse sums
connection: Look for modular inverses after solving the factor congruence for one variable and compare the resulting sums with Kloosterman-type phases.
why: Inverse phases are a concrete analytic structure, although a useful bound must be checked.
first_step: Derive the additive-character expansion for one factor congruence and identify its phase exactly.

title: Voronoi-style dualization
connection: Check whether divisor-weighted progressions in an ES count fit a summation formula that exchanges long and short ranges.
why: A dual expression could reveal cancellation or a useful geometric interpretation.
first_step: Write the smoothed divisor sum explicitly and check available Voronoi formulas against its modulus dependence.

title: Shifted convolution of auxiliary integers
connection: Compare divisor counts of 4Cp+1 and 4Dp+1 as a shifted or linearly related convolution.
why: These correlations describe redundancy between certificate lines more precisely than independence heuristics.
first_step: Expand the mixed divisor count for C=1,D=2 and identify the underlying linear relation.

title: Local densities as fingerprints
connection: Compute exact residue-level densities for several certificate families and use the vector of densities as a fingerprint of p.
why: Local fingerprints might predict complementary families without asserting a local-global principle.
first_step: Enumerate admissible parameter tuples modulo 8,9,5,7 for three exact identities.

title: Singular-series fluctuations
connection: Build a candidate Euler-product heuristic from local densities and compare it with observed certificate counts.
why: A varying local factor may explain low-count primes better than a single average.
first_step: Compute truncated products using primes up to 31 and compare with bounded-search counts.

title: Exceptional-prime clustering
connection: Study whether primes with few bounded certificates cluster in arithmetic progressions or short intervals.
why: Structure in the tail could suggest targeted constructions rather than more uniform averaging.
first_step: Define one fixed search budget and compare the bottom count decile across residue classes and intervals.

title: High moments of certificate counts
connection: Expand third and fourth moments of a bounded certificate count to distinguish thin tails from heavy correlations.
why: Higher moments retain information that the average and variance can miss.
first_step: Compute the first four empirical moments with the same cutoff for all sampled primes.

title: Factorial moments of distinct witnesses
connection: Count ordered tuples of genuinely distinct witnesses rather than powers that include repeated certificates.
why: Factorial moments isolate multiplicity and can test a Poisson-like model cleanly.
first_step: Canonicalize denominator triples and calculate the first three factorial moments by prime range.

title: Janson-style avoidance models
connection: Model bounded auxiliary choices as witness events and investigate whether an avoidance inequality can be justified from their dependencies.
why: A bound below one on an actual finite avoidance probability would certify at least one witness for that fixed instance.
first_step: Specify a finite probability space of auxiliary choices and compute all pairwise event intersections for small p.

title: Decay of parameter correlations
connection: Measure how correlation between successes at C and D depends on gcd(C,D), distance, and shared small factors.
why: Arithmetic dependence may have a usable organization even without independence.
first_step: Estimate pairwise success correlations for C,D≤40 after grouping pairs by gcd.

title: Dependency graphs for witnesses
connection: Create a graph connecting certificate searches that share prime factors or congruence constraints.
why: Graph sparsity could support more accurate probability models and search schedules.
first_step: For a fixed sample, compare a shared-factor graph with measured success correlations.

title: Lopsided dependence of failures
connection: Ask whether failure events exhibit one-sided dependence more favorable than their raw correlations suggest.
why: Avoidance estimates sometimes use conditional probabilities rather than symmetric independence.
first_step: Compute conditional failure frequencies for pairs and triples of parameter choices without extrapolating to a theorem.

title: Entropy of divisor residues
connection: Measure how rapidly the residue distribution spreads as prime-power factors are added to a divisor set.
why: Entropy gives a quantitative description of concentration in a proper subgroup or coset.
first_step: Convolve the two-choice residue measures factor by factor for small factored auxiliary integers.

title: Smooth auxiliary values
connection: Favor parameters for which the p-tied integer has many small prime factors, then inspect whether their divisor residues cover the target.
why: Smoothness supplies many selectable factors but does not by itself settle residue coverage.
first_step: Search C≤100 for primes below 1000 and correlate smoothness with target-residue success.

title: Rough–smooth complementary constructions
connection: Pair a construction exploiting many small factors with one exploiting a single large complementary factor.
why: The two regimes may produce genuinely different certificate mechanisms.
first_step: Partition auxiliary values by largest-prime-factor ratio and compare the successful denominator shapes.

title: Least quadratic nonresidue steering
connection: Use small quadratic nonresidues to choose auxiliary parameters that escape symbol restrictions of one family.
why: A character witness supplies arithmetic information beyond p modulo a fixed integer.
first_step: For each sampled prime, correlate its least nonresidue with the smallest successful auxiliary parameter.

title: Short character-sum templates
connection: Check whether short character-sum estimates can force one useful parameter value within a moving interval.
why: This is relevant only after a certificate condition has been reduced to a character pattern.
first_step: Derive a concrete character-pattern sufficient condition, then check whether Burgess-type estimates apply to its interval and polynomial.

title: Prime divisors in prescribed classes
connection: Study which prime-factor residue patterns of 4Cp+1 are sufficient to produce a target divisor.
why: Some successes may follow from one or two factors rather than the whole divisor set.
first_step: Enumerate minimal sufficient factor-residue multisets for small moduli.

title: Splitting fields of auxiliary polynomials
connection: For polynomial subfamilies of auxiliary values, relate factor-residue behavior to splitting in explicitly computed number fields.
why: Field structure may organize observed factor patterns, though integer prime divisors need separate analysis.
first_step: Compute a splitting field for one quadratic auxiliary polynomial and state precisely which finite-field splitting event is relevant.

title: Chebotarev questions for family selection
connection: Ask whether a family-selection condition is a Frobenius condition in a fixed finite extension.
why: If it is, an existing distribution theorem might describe which primes select that family, not automatically all primes.
first_step: For one proposed selector, build the extension and check whether its predicate really depends only on Frobenius.

title: Pretentious character diagnostics
connection: Compare stubborn divisor-residue biases with multiplicative functions that mimic simple characters on small primes.
why: A structured bias could suggest a complementary family tailored to that character.
first_step: Compute distances between empirical factor-sign patterns and a small library of Dirichlet characters.

title: Reciprocity-induced correlation
connection: Track how reciprocity couples residue information about p and its auxiliary factors.
why: Treating those symbols as independent would obscure exact constraints that might guide construction.
first_step: Tabulate both directions of Legendre symbols for successful certificates and derive the forced sign relation.

title: Additive energy of log-residue sets
connection: In a cyclic residue group, take discrete logs of available factor residues and measure additive energy.
why: High energy signals a structured subset-product obstruction that can be described concretely.
first_step: Compute sumset sizes and energies for factor-log sets at moduli with cyclic unit group.

title: Sum–product mixing across parameters
connection: Compare multiplicative divisor generation with additive changes in the auxiliary parameter.
why: Alternating two different operations may escape concentration that persists under either alone.
first_step: Build a small state graph with factor multiplication and valid parameter-shift edges, checking each edge algebraically.

title: Expander-inspired residue walks
connection: Use random walks on residue groups generated by available prime factors to estimate how hard a target class is to reach.
why: A walk model can suggest search strategies even when available factor multiplicities prevent unrestricted walks.
first_step: Compare unrestricted walk mixing with exact bounded-multiplicity divisor reachability.

title: Spectral gaps of certificate transitions
connection: Construct a finite transition matrix from verified certificate transformations and inspect its bottlenecks.
why: A spectral picture may identify missing moves or separated families, not prove connectivity on its own.
first_step: Enumerate bounded certificates for one p and compute transition components before estimating eigenvalues.

title: Bohr-set parameter windows
connection: Interpret simultaneous near-integral rational expressions in a parametrization as a finite Bohr-set-like condition.
why: Approximate alignment can identify intervals where exact divisibility is worth testing.
first_step: For two explicit rational coefficient conditions, plot simultaneous fractional-part windows over the parameter range.

title: Polynomial recurrence selectors
connection: Ask whether a parameter sequence chosen by polynomial recurrence repeatedly enters a sufficient residue pattern.
why: Recurrence could replace an unstructured search if its visits can be made effective.
first_step: Choose one exact sufficient congruence pattern and compute visits of quadratic parameter sequences modulo its modulus.

title: Torus rotations for denominator rounding
connection: Express the rounding error of p divided by a small parameter as a fractional-part coordinate.
why: Related rotations may coordinate two rounding choices whose errors must cancel.
first_step: Derive the exact residual after two floor-based denominator choices and plot the error pair.

title: Discrepancy of admissible parameters
connection: Measure deviation of successful parameter residues from uniformity across intervals.
why: A useful discrepancy bound could turn a dense parameter set into an explicit interval witness.
first_step: For a fixed family, compute interval discrepancy at several cutoffs and distinguish local biases from global drift.

title: Beatty-sequence denominators
connection: Choose candidate denominators from complementary floor sequences and inspect exact reciprocal residuals.
why: Complementary sequences offer a systematic way to couple rounding errors without claiming an identity.
first_step: For slopes with simple quadratic irrational values, test the first two denominators and factor the residual numerator.

title: CRT covering radius
connection: View simultaneous modular exclusions as a periodic subset of integers and ask about its largest parameter gap.
why: The largest gap directly measures how far an auxiliary search may have to travel.
first_step: For several small modulus sets, enumerate the allowed residues over one period and compute maximum gaps.

title: Sieve parity diagnostics
connection: Check which certificate predicates depend only on roughness and which depend on the parity or residue of factor products.
why: This identifies information a chosen sieve model must retain, without discarding the connection.
first_step: Construct two auxiliary integers with matching small-prime divisibility data but different target-divisor behavior.

title: Vector-valued sieving
connection: Keep several certificate-family weights simultaneously rather than collapsing them into one scalar sieve weight.
why: Different families may respond differently to the same local exclusion.
first_step: Tabulate a vector of local survival indicators for three families modulo the first five primes.

title: Dense-model questions for divisor residues
connection: Ask whether a normalized divisor-residue measure resembles a simpler measure on the test functions relevant to ES.
why: Only the relevant tests need approximation, so a tailored model might be more useful than global uniformity.
first_step: Specify a finite test-function family and solve for a simple measure matching its moments.

title: Transference from a model problem
connection: Design a finite-field or random-factor analogue where a three-term certificate statement is tractable, then identify exactly what transfers.
why: A model can isolate the deterministic ingredient missing from a heuristic.
first_step: Prove a small finite-group subset-product statement and list which hypotheses actual auxiliary factors satisfy.

title: Logarithmic weights tuned to rare witnesses
connection: Weight certificates by divisor size or auxiliary complexity to reduce domination by primes with many easy witnesses.
why: A better weight may make sparse cases more visible in moment calculations.
first_step: Compare unweighted counts with reciprocal-divisor and inverse-multiplicity weights on the same prime sample.

title: Rare prime strata as separate models
connection: Partition primes by combinations of small character values and build separate count models for sparse strata.
why: Mixture distributions can hide strong structure in an exceptional tail.
first_step: Choose three small character labels and compare the full count histogram within each nonempty stratum.

title: Arithmetic-progression packets
connection: Search for groups of nearby prime parameters in one progression that share a certificate template with varying integer coefficients.
why: Shared templates might support an induction-like construction or explain coverage bursts.
first_step: For a fixed modulus, collect consecutive primes and fit only symbolically verifiable affine parameter relations.

title: Divisor collision counting
connection: Count pairs of auxiliary values sharing a useful divisor and interpret the resulting linear relation between their parameters.
why: Collisions can create transfer rules between searches rather than merely redundant counts.
first_step: Solve d dividing both 4Cp+1 and 4Dp+1 and classify the resulting restrictions on C−D.

title: Complement-residue bias correction
connection: Compare a naive uniform divisor-residue heuristic with the exact complementary-divisor pairing constraints.
why: Correcting this built-in dependence may sharpen predictions of rare zero counts.
first_step: Derive the paired-residue count identities for small moduli and fit a constrained null model.

title: Moment inversion for zero counts
connection: Use finite-support moment bounds to estimate the possible mass at zero under measured or proved count moments.
why: This makes the distinction between average abundance and universal positivity explicit without rejecting the approach.
first_step: Solve the small linear program maximizing zero mass subject to the first three empirical moments.

title: Uniform parameter thresholds
connection: Track how the smallest successful auxiliary cutoff grows separately in each arithmetic stratum.
why: A precise growth target can suggest which analytic estimate would actually be sufficient.
first_step: Compute running maxima of the least successful C and report them against log p and powers of p, with bounded-search caveats.

title: Witness hypergraphs
connection: Build a hypergraph whose vertices are auxiliary choices and whose edges are jointly compatible pieces of a certificate.
why: Compatibility may be more naturally expressed by small tuples than by one successful parameter.
first_step: For one exact parametrization, separate its constraints into three pieces and enumerate compatible triples for a small prime.

title: Flow networks for factor allocation
connection: Model allocation of prime-power factors to denominator components as a capacitated network when the valuation constraints permit it.
why: Flow feasibility can solve the allocation part exactly, leaving residue constraints visible.
first_step: For a factored small auxiliary integer, derive factor capacities and compare feasible flows with actual certificates.

title: Determinantal matching encodings
connection: Ask whether a restricted certificate family can be encoded as perfect matchings with a nonvanishing determinant witness.
why: A matching formulation could import exact combinatorial certificates, but the encoding must avoid spurious solutions.
first_step: Construct a bipartite compatibility graph for a toy factor-allocation problem and test which matchings yield ES triples.

title: Matroids for family diversity
connection: Treat residue tests supplied by candidate families as feature vectors and use independence to choose a diverse search portfolio.
why: Linear independence is a cheap surrogate for avoiding many near-identical families.
first_step: Build a binary family-by-test matrix on small primes and compare independent subsets with greedy coverage subsets.

title: Transversal numbers of failure patterns
connection: Represent each observed failure pattern by the families that repair it and study the minimum hitting set.
why: This extracts complementary mechanisms rather than just ranking individually successful identities.
first_step: Compute a minimum hitting set for a bounded family-prime incidence matrix.

title: VC dimension of certificate families
connection: View each parametrized identity as a subset of sampled primes and estimate the combinatorial complexity of that set system.
why: Low complexity might explain why small representative samples reveal much of the coverage structure.
first_step: Search for shattered subsets of size up to five in a bounded incidence matrix.

title: Epsilon-net search portfolios
connection: Ask whether a small portfolio can hit every sufficiently large witness set in a specified finite parameter universe.
why: An epsilon-net statement would be a finite search guarantee, not a proof for all primes without uniform hypotheses.
first_step: Define the witness-set universe for a bounded experiment and compare greedy nets with random samples.

title: Discrepancy-balanced family splits
connection: Color certificate families into two portfolios whose coverage counts stay close across sampled primes.
why: Balanced splits can reveal genuine diversity and create independent-looking diagnostic datasets.
first_step: Solve a small discrepancy-minimization problem on the family-prime incidence matrix.

title: Proof-producing set cover
connection: Compress a finite verified range into exact identity templates plus a certified set-cover computation.
why: The output remains a finite-range proof, but it makes coverage mechanisms auditable.
first_step: Take 100 primes and export the chosen identities with exact substitution witnesses for each covered prime.

title: Sunflower patterns among constraints
connection: Search for families of certificate conditions sharing a common core and disjoint extra congruence requirements.
why: A sunflower structure may identify a reusable common lemma with several interchangeable completions.
first_step: Represent each small family by its set of atomic congruence conditions and detect common-core collections.

title: Ramsey extraction of parameter patterns
connection: Color small parameter tuples by which certificate mechanism succeeds and look for structured monochromatic configurations.
why: Regular patterns can suggest identities, provided each conjectured identity is checked algebraically.
first_step: Color a bounded parameter grid and search for rectangles whose four corners share a symbolic template.

title: Arithmetic progressions inside witness sets
connection: Look for long arithmetic progressions of successful auxiliary parameters and derive the conditions responsible.
why: Progressions may signal a hidden congruence family rather than random abundance.
first_step: For fixed small primes, find maximal progressions of successful C and compare their differences with the factorization of p−1.

title: Combinatorial word lines
connection: Encode elementary matrix choices as words and ask whether varying one wildcard block preserves an ES-relevant identity.
why: A combinatorial line could package many related certificates into a single construction.
first_step: Enumerate short matrix words with one repeated wildcard and symbolically compute their coordinate expressions.

title: Residue graph homomorphisms
connection: Map an integral certificate-transition graph to its reductions modulo several small integers.
why: Fibers and missing lifts can reveal exactly what information a residue graph forgets.
first_step: Construct the reduction map for a bounded transition graph and inspect fibers of successful residue states.

title: Base-digit automata
connection: Track a certificate equation digit by digit with carries in a fixed base.
why: Polynomial equalities admit finite carry descriptions under bounded-width restrictions, yielding concrete restricted models.
first_step: Build a base-two carry checker for bounded denominator triples and minimize its state graph.

title: Automatic pattern diagnostics
connection: Test whether experimentally observed family selectors have low-complexity digit behavior.
why: A short automaton would suggest a recursive selector, though finite data cannot establish automaticity.
first_step: Infer minimal automata from initial selector labels and test them on a disjoint larger range.

title: Regular languages of valid matrix words
connection: Describe congruence-admissible matrix words by a finite automaton and distinguish this from their unbounded integer values.
why: Congruence admissibility is genuinely finite-state, providing a rigorous symbolic skeleton.
first_step: Build an automaton for elementary matrices modulo 8 with accepting states matching one required coordinate condition.

title: Weighted automata for word height
connection: Add costs measuring coefficient size or word length to the congruence automaton.
why: Shortest accepted paths can find economical candidate certificates while respecting exact finite-state constraints.
first_step: Run shortest-path search with logarithmic coefficient cost and compare candidates against direct enumeration.

title: Synchronizing words for congruences
connection: Ask whether a shared suffix of elementary operations sends many residue states into a useful target set.
why: Such a suffix would be a reusable congruence repair mechanism, if allowed moves preserve the needed algebra.
first_step: Enumerate short suffixes in the modular transition system and measure the size of their target preimages.

title: Carry cellular automata
connection: View the multiplication and addition in the cleared ES equation as local carry interactions on digit strings.
why: Local update rules may reveal impossible digit patterns or efficient branch propagation.
first_step: Implement a bounded-width carry propagation diagram for a toy prime and compare its pruning with naive digit search.

title: Finite-state rational transducers
connection: Search for digit-wise rules mapping p to candidate denominator digits with bounded carry memory.
why: A successful rule on a well-defined input language could become an explicit infinite family.
first_step: Synthesize a transducer for one already verified congruence family and inspect which extra states are needed to enlarge its domain.

title: Digit lifting of identities
connection: Try extending a certificate for a truncated base expansion of p when one more digit is appended.
why: This is an induction proposal with exact algebraic correction terms, not an assumption that prime prefixes behave well.
first_step: Substitute p′=bp+r and x′=bx+a into the cleared equation and solve the first correction constraints.

title: Transfer matrices for bounded factor states
connection: Count admissible divisor selections with a transfer matrix whose state records residue and used multiplicities.
why: This exactly computes bounded subset-product counts and exposes repeated local blocks.
first_step: Build a transfer matrix for each prime-power factor and multiply them for one auxiliary integer.

title: Multivariate certificate generating functions
connection: Weight certificates by denominator height, gcd type, and parameter size in a formal generating series.
why: Different projections of one series can compare search costs and arithmetic strata.
first_step: Compute a truncated series for p=13 and inspect which coefficients are invariant under denominator permutation.

title: Partitions of the reciprocal mass
connection: Connect ES to restricted partition problems after multiplying by a common denominator L: 4L/p=L/x+L/y+L/z.
why: The summands are divisors of L, so this is an exact three-part divisor partition when p divides L.
first_step: For several small multiples L of p, enumerate three-divisor partitions of 4L/p.

title: Restricted additive bases of divisors
connection: Ask when the divisor set of a chosen common denominator is an additive basis for the specific target 4L/p.
why: This reframes the problem as a constrained three-sum problem with tunable ambient integer L.
first_step: For L=p times a small smooth number, compute D(L)+D(L)+D(L) near the target.

title: Partition reciprocity as a sanity tool
connection: Compare positive and nonnegative lattice-point counts in polyhedral relaxations of denominator constraints.
why: Boundary corrections may identify which apparent certificates are merely zero or infinite-denominator artifacts.
first_step: Construct a simple linearized divisor-allocation polytope and compare interior with closed lattice-point counts.

title: Ehrhart families of auxiliary polytopes
connection: When a parametrization reduces to linear inequalities and congruences, study its integer-point count as the bounds dilate.
why: Quasipolynomial counts can give exact finite-family information without addressing nonlinear cases automatically.
first_step: Isolate one linear parameter region and compute its first several dilation counts.

title: Inside-out polytopes for exclusions
connection: Represent linear positivity regions with forbidden congruence hyperplanes or boundary subspaces in a lifted lattice.
why: This separates the bulk feasible region from thin degeneracies.
first_step: For a small linear family, list forbidden hyperplanes and count remaining lattice points at low dilation.

title: Integer programming with witness cuts
connection: Use integer programming on a linearized auxiliary formulation, adding exact cuts learned from failed modular assignments.
why: A solver can discover useful constraints while all final witnesses remain directly checkable.
first_step: Linearize one bounded factor-allocation model and add only cuts proved from its congruence equations.

title: Markov bases for certificate fibers
connection: Seek finite move sets connecting all nonnegative solutions of a fixed linearized parameter constraint.
why: Connectivity of the linear fiber could reduce enumeration before nonlinear conditions are imposed.
first_step: Compute a kernel basis for a toy exponent-allocation matrix and test which moves preserve positivity.

title: Toric ideals of monomial substitutions
connection: Encode multiplicative relations among denominator components as binomial equations and study their toric moves.
why: Toric structure may organize equivalent factorizations without confusing them with the additive ES condition.
first_step: For one gcd parametrization, list its monomial map and derive elementary binomial relations.

title: Contingency-table factor allocations
connection: Arrange prime valuations in a table indexed by factors and denominator components, with row totals fixed.
why: This creates a familiar integer-fiber problem for the multiplicative part of certificate construction.
first_step: Enumerate valuation tables for an auxiliary integer with three prime factors and compare their induced congruence outcomes.

title: Matrix-tree determinants
connection: Compare determinant expressions from the forest formulation with graph Laplacian cofactors.
why: A graph realization could make positivity or combinatorial multiplicity transparent.
first_step: Construct small weighted trees and check which Laplacian minors reproduce short tuv−u−v expressions.

title: Sandpile groups as residue containers
connection: Investigate whether cokernels of Laplacians appearing in certificate encodings organize denominator congruences.
why: The finite abelian group retains integral information beyond a real determinant.
first_step: For a candidate graph encoding, compute its Smith normal form and compare invariant factors with certificate moduli.

title: Electrical network interpretation
connection: Interpret a denominator or continued-fraction identity as series-parallel resistance reduction.
why: Exact rational network laws may suggest composition operations whose integrality can then be checked.
first_step: Translate short continued fractions into resistor networks and mark operations preserving the required residue classes.

title: Nonbacktracking certificate walks
connection: Forbid immediate inverse moves in a certificate graph and compare the resulting exploration with unrestricted walks.
why: Avoiding trivial reversals may expose genuine cycles and increase search diversity.
first_step: Enumerate nonbacktracking paths of length at most eight in a small verified transition graph.

title: Interlacing under adding families
connection: Compare spectra of finite incidence matrices before and after adding a new certificate family.
why: Spectral changes may quantify genuinely new coverage directions rather than raw success counts.
first_step: Compute singular values of a family-prime matrix and rank additions by their effect on the smallest nonzero values.

title: Graph covers and congruence refinement
connection: View reduction modulo a larger modulus as a refinement of a smaller residue-state graph.
why: Covering-like behavior could make iterative modular analysis systematic; exceptional fibers are equally informative.
first_step: Compare transition graphs modulo 4 and 8 and classify how vertices and edges lift.

title: Random spanning-tree exploration
connection: Sample spanning trees of a finite certificate graph to obtain nonredundant exploration routes.
why: The tree removes cycles while retaining reachability within the sampled component.
first_step: Compare the distinct parameter regions visited by depth-first search and random-tree-guided search under equal budgets.

title: Discrete Morse reductions
connection: Assign a combinatorial gradient to a bounded certificate complex and collapse redundant regions.
why: A reduced complex might isolate the essential obstructions to moving between certificate families.
first_step: Build a small complex from compatible local moves and test elementary collapses with explicit free-face checks.

title: Persistent topology of bounded searches
connection: Filter a point cloud of certificates by height and examine components and cycles as the cutoff grows.
why: Persistent features can suggest missing transformations; they are exploratory descriptors, not arithmetic obstructions.
first_step: For one p, compute only sparse graph-based persistence of certificate shapes at several height thresholds.

title: Nerves of parametrization charts
connection: Construct the nerve whose vertices are exact parametrizations and whose simplices record shared certificates.
why: Intersections may expose a small core of identities linking otherwise separate approaches.
first_step: Compute pairwise and triple intersections for five small parametrization families over a finite prime sample.

title: Rewriting confluence
connection: Orient exact identity transformations and ask whether different reduction paths reach a common normal form.
why: Confluence would make duplicate removal and family comparison mathematically cleaner.
first_step: For a finite rule set, enumerate critical overlaps and check equality by cross multiplication.

title: Termination orders for identity search
connection: Seek a well-founded monomial or lexicographic order that decreases under selected ES transformations.
why: A genuine termination argument could turn heuristic rewriting into a reliable normalization procedure.
first_step: Try lexicographic orders on denominator height and gcd data for three verified rewrite rules.

title: Petri nets for denominator resources
connection: Model valuation transfers under exact identity moves as token transitions between denominator components.
why: Conservation laws in the net may reveal which transformations can or cannot connect two families.
first_step: Derive a token transition from one exact move and compute its linear invariants.

title: Scheduling complementary searches
connection: Treat each family as a job with a measurable cost and a prime-dependent success profile.
why: Scheduling can improve exploratory reach without confusing computational efficiency with a proof.
first_step: Compare round-robin, least-cost-first, and residue-conditioned schedules on a held-out prime interval.

title: Combinatorial games on residual fractions
connection: Define legal moves as exact split-and-merge operations and winning positions as positive three-term decompositions.
why: A strategy theorem on a specified class of positions could produce constructive identities.
first_step: Write precise game rules, enumerate small positions, and look for a decreasing potential on winning strategies.

title: Tilings that encode reciprocal sums
connection: Represent unit fractions as areas of equal-height rectangles after choosing a common grid.
why: A carefully constrained tiling model may turn divisibility and positivity into visible local conditions.
first_step: For a fixed L divisible by p, draw three rectangles of areas L/x,L/y,L/z summing to 4L/p and record grid restrictions.

title: Rhythmic subdivisions as identity generators
connection: Translate exact unit-fraction splitting into subdivisions of a common rhythmic cycle, then search for regroupings into three parts.
why: The musical picture is only a representation of rational identities, but may prompt overlooked regroupings.
first_step: Enumerate subdivisions of a 60-slot cycle and retain only regroupings that verify an exact three-unit-fraction equality.

title: Spin systems for factor selection
connection: Assign a binary spin to each available prime factor and make the total residue the observable of the selected product.
why: This is an exact finite statistical-mechanics model of divisor selection when multiplicities are tracked.
first_step: For a squarefree auxiliary integer, compute the residue distribution by both spin enumeration and divisor enumeration.

title: Certificate partition functions
connection: Introduce a fugacity for auxiliary size and form a finite partition function whose coefficients count verified certificates.
why: Different fugacities emphasize economical witnesses or high multiplicity without changing the underlying exact count.
first_step: Compute the partition polynomial for a small prime and compare its low-degree coefficients across primes.

title: Zeros of counting polynomials
connection: Study complex zeros of finite certificate-generating polynomials as descriptors of changes in count structure.
why: Root geometry can distinguish count distributions, but no phase-transition or positivity theorem is assumed.
first_step: Compute roots of low-degree count polynomials and check whether unusual root patterns correlate with sparse witness sets.

title: Cluster expansions for factor dependence
connection: Group interacting prime-factor selections into connected clusters instead of treating them as independent residue choices.
why: A convergent or finite exact expansion could organize corrections to naive randomness.
first_step: For an auxiliary integer with at most six distinct factors, calculate connected correlation terms explicitly.

title: Replica overlap diagnostics
connection: Take two independently sampled certificates for the same p and measure how many factor choices or denominator components they share.
why: Overlap distributions distinguish a broad witness space from many variants of one mechanism.
first_step: Sample bounded certificates uniformly after deduplication and histogram their factor-overlap sizes.

title: Cavity messages on factor graphs
connection: Represent local valuation and congruence constraints as a factor graph and pass approximate marginal messages.
why: Belief propagation can suggest assignments, while exact substitution verifies every output.
first_step: Build a small factor graph for residue-factor selection and compare message marginals with exhaustive enumeration.

title: Frustration in congruence loops
connection: Identify cycles of local congruence requirements that cannot all be satisfied within a chosen family.
why: Minimal inconsistent loops may indicate which single condition a new family should replace.
first_step: Extract a minimal unsatisfiable set of congruences from a small failed parameter ansatz.

title: Search-budget phase diagrams
connection: Plot witness existence and multiplicity against two independent cutoffs, such as C and allowed denominator height.
why: A two-dimensional diagram may distinguish families that look identical under a single budget.
first_step: For a fixed prime sample, compute coarse grids of success rates over both cutoffs.

title: Finite-size scaling as a falsifiable heuristic
connection: Compare rescaled distributions of least witness cost across increasing prime ranges.
why: A scaling collapse could propose a growth law; failure of collapse is also informative.
first_step: Fit the scaling on one prime range and test it on a larger disjoint range with identical search rules.

title: Renormalization by eliminating small factors
connection: Integrate out the choices involving the smallest prime factors to obtain an effective residue distribution for the remaining factors.
why: This is exact convolution on a finite group before any approximation is introduced.
first_step: Eliminate prime factors one at a time and track support size, entropy, and target mass.

title: Modular energy landscapes
connection: Define an integer energy from violated congruences and exact residual divisibility, with zero energy reserved for checked certificates.
why: The landscape may reveal useful local moves and traps rather than merely a solver score.
first_step: For a bounded parameter box, enumerate energies and locate local minima under unit-coordinate changes.

title: Annealing with exact repairs
connection: Combine stochastic descent on a congruence energy with deterministic repair of one remaining divisibility condition.
why: A repair step ties the physical analogy to exact arithmetic output.
first_step: Implement a toy annealer on one residual parametrization and verify every reported zero by integer arithmetic.

title: Parallel tempering across families
connection: Allow searches at different energy scales or in different parametrization charts to exchange states through exact chart maps.
why: Exchanges may overcome family-specific traps if the maps are valid and reversible on their domains.
first_step: For two charts with a known overlap, test state exchanges on bounded rational points before imposing integrality.

title: Density of states near valid certificates
connection: Count parameter assignments by exact residual size and divisibility defect rather than only success or failure.
why: Near-zero abundance might suggest a correction lemma or reveal that approximate solutions are misleading.
first_step: Compute the joint histogram of residual numerator and gcd defect for a small parameter box.

title: Rare-event importance sampling
connection: Bias experiments toward primes and parameter regions with few known witnesses, correcting weights when estimating distributions.
why: This explores difficult tails more efficiently without claiming the biased sample is representative.
first_step: Construct a proposal distribution based on small-prime residue labels and record explicit sampling weights.

title: Quenched versus annealed witness counts
connection: Compare the average logarithm of positive count regularizations with the logarithm of the average count across primes.
why: Their gap measures domination by unusually easy instances and helps diagnose misleading averages.
first_step: Compute both statistics for log(1+N(p)) and log of 1 plus the mean N(p) at fixed cutoffs.

title: Random-matrix baselines for family incidence
connection: Compare singular values of the actual family-prime incidence matrix with matrices preserving its row and column sums.
why: This can detect collective arithmetic structure beyond individual family success rates.
first_step: Generate degree-preserving shuffled matrices and compare their leading singular values with the original.

title: Arithmetic spectral outliers
connection: Associate a finite operator with residue transitions and ask whether spectral outliers align with quadratic-character sectors.
why: A character decomposition can make a spectral pattern arithmetically interpretable.
first_step: Diagonalize a small convolution operator by characters and compare its modes with observed success biases.

title: Quantum-walk-inspired exploration
connection: Compare coherent-walk-inspired search heuristics with classical walks on a finite residue graph, without assuming hardware speedups.
why: Interference patterns may suggest new deterministic orderings of candidate residues.
first_step: Simulate a very small unitary walk and compare the high-amplitude states with shortest target-reaching paths.

title: Adiabatic encodings of bounded ES search
connection: Encode a bounded certificate search as a finite polynomial binary optimization problem and inspect its low-energy states.
why: The encoding itself may expose useful constraints regardless of whether quantum optimization is practical.
first_step: Build an exact tiny QUBO with explicit carry ancillas and verify its ground states by exhaustive enumeration.

title: Tensor-network contraction of residue constraints
connection: Represent factor choices and congruence checks as small tensors and contract along a low-width graph.
why: Contraction order can exploit sparse dependencies in exact witness counting.
first_step: Construct a residue-selection tensor network for at most ten factors and compare contraction widths.

title: Tensor rank of identity families
connection: Represent coefficients of a bounded-degree ES ansatz as a tensor and seek low-rank structure.
why: Low-rank decompositions can propose separable parameter substitutions that are then checked symbolically.
first_step: Form the coefficient tensor of one cleared ansatz and inspect rank-one or rank-two decompositions over the rationals.

title: Holographic changes of basis
connection: Test whether a basis change simplifies local tensors in a finite certificate constraint network.
why: Some encodings become easier after transforming the local representation, but all arithmetic constraints must survive.
first_step: Apply small invertible basis changes to a toy residue tensor and compare sparsity and contraction cost.

title: QRT-style invariant curves
connection: Look for birational two-variable maps preserving an exact auxiliary curve and producing new rational certificates.
why: An invariant map could generate recurrent families if integrality and positivity are controlled.
first_step: For a quadratic slice, derive a root-switch map and compute a rational invariant or show none appears at low degree.

title: Lax-pair discovery as an algebraic search
connection: Ask whether a certificate-preserving transformation admits a matrix conjugation description with invariant characteristic polynomial.
why: A Lax representation would expose conserved quantities, not by itself guarantee positive integer orbits.
first_step: For one verified rational map, search two-by-two matrix entries of low degree satisfying the conjugation equation.

title: Toda-like recurrences of continuants
connection: Compare determinant recurrences of tridiagonal matrices with short continued-fraction certificate expressions.
why: Shared determinant algebra may suggest bilinear recurrence identities useful for composition.
first_step: Compute adjacent tridiagonal minors symbolically and test their identities against a short continuant parametrization.

title: Refactorization and Yang–Baxter leads
connection: Search for different factorizations of the same elementary matrix product that exchange parameter triples.
why: Refactorization produces exact rational transformations whose congruence effects can be examined.
first_step: Solve a three-factor matrix equality in two different orders and check whether the resulting map has an ES-admissible domain.

title: Star–triangle arithmetic moves
connection: Test the electrical star–triangle transformation as a source of rational three-variable identities with controlled denominator factors.
why: The network equality is exact, but integer preservation needs explicit extra conditions.
first_step: Write the star–triangle formulas and solve their integrality requirements for small positive integer inputs.

title: Symplectic coordinates for matrix words
connection: Use the area-preserving action of SL₂ on pairs of coordinates to track certificate-related invariants.
why: An invariant determinant can constrain possible moves more cleanly than expanded polynomials.
first_step: Choose two column vectors from a short word and compute which parameter changes preserve their determinant and residue labels.

title: Modular geodesic coding
connection: Compare continued-fraction certificate words with symbolic codes of geodesic segments on the modular surface.
why: Geometric coding may organize word length and cusp excursions, while the ES condition remains arithmetic.
first_step: Translate several short certificate words into matrices and compute their fixed points and trace types.

title: Horocycle sampling of congruence states
connection: Study elementary unipotent matrix orbits modulo small integers and their integer-height growth.
why: These are explicit orbits that could generate systematic candidate families.
first_step: Enumerate products of two unipotent flows modulo 16 and track the least integer height realizing each target state.

title: Homogeneous-flow shrinking targets
connection: Rephrase finding short lattice vectors with extra congruences as a target-hitting problem in a family of lattices.
why: The formulation may identify what effective recurrence statement would suffice.
first_step: Write the exact target region for one lattice encoding and calculate how its volume changes with p.

title: Skew products coupling size and residue
connection: Track a real size coordinate together with a finite residue state under a certificate-related recurrence.
why: This separates growth from arithmetic admissibility while keeping their interaction explicit.
first_step: Build the skew-product map for a short Euclidean or matrix recurrence and plot admissible returns.

title: Interval-exchange selectors
connection: Use interval maps associated with rational approximation to partition parameter choices into symbolic regimes.
why: A finite partition might yield a small list of exact denominator formulas on each regime.
first_step: Compute return itineraries for a simple interval map and test whether an exact residual formula is constant in symbolic type.

title: Periodic-orbit certificate families
connection: Search for parameter recurrences with periodic residue states and nonperiodic integer growth.
why: A periodic modular pattern can preserve admissibility along an infinite arithmetic orbit.
first_step: For one exact recurrence, enumerate cycles modulo 8 and verify which lifted initial points remain positive integers.

title: Return-time distributions
connection: Measure first visits to admissible residue states in deterministic certificate-generating dynamics.
why: Return-time tails are directly connected to the cost of the resulting search procedure.
first_step: For several initial states, record first-hit times and compare them with orbit component sizes.

title: Arithmetic cocycles
connection: Record a multiplicative scale factor and a congruence correction along each matrix or continued-fraction move.
why: The cocycle may reveal telescoping products that enforce integrality after a whole word.
first_step: Compute the scale cocycle for three verified moves and search short loops with unit total correction.

title: Escape to the cusp
connection: Interpret unusually large minimal denominators as possible degeneration of an associated lattice basis.
why: This can distinguish missing certificates from certificates hidden in highly anisotropic regions.
first_step: For difficult bounded instances, compute successive minima of a relevant small lattice and compare them with denominator imbalance.

title: Adelic height bookkeeping
connection: Combine real denominator size with p-adic valuation penalties in a single explicitly defined height.
why: A balanced height might reveal a descent invisible to the archimedean maximum alone.
first_step: Define a height on one rational parametrization and calculate its change under two exact transformations.

title: Arithmetic tori from norm-one units
connection: Use norm-one units to move along a norm-equation slice while preserving its right-hand side.
why: The remaining question becomes whether the orbit reaches the positivity and congruence region needed for ES.
first_step: For a small real quadratic norm equation, compute unit-orbit residues modulo the required modulus.

title: p-adic dynamics of parameter maps
connection: Iterate an exact rational parameter transformation over residue rings and inspect attracting or periodic classes.
why: Stable modular behavior could support iterative congruence repair before real positivity is addressed.
first_step: For a verified map, enumerate its defined orbits modulo 3² and 3³ and compare lifting patterns.

title: Convex relaxations of bounded searches
connection: Relax selected bilinear constraints using valid convex envelopes inside a finite parameter box.
why: The relaxation can prune impossible boxes or reveal promising corners, without supplying integer witnesses by itself.
first_step: Apply McCormick envelopes to one bounded auxiliary equation and compare feasible boxes with exact enumeration.

title: Reciprocal convexity bounds
connection: Use convexity of 1/t to derive necessary bounds on denominator sums and imbalance within a chosen search region.
why: These bounds are elementary and can reduce search without risking false sufficiency claims.
first_step: Derive Jensen and tangent-line bounds for ordered x≤y≤z satisfying the reciprocal sum.

title: Harmonic–arithmetic mean constraints
connection: Relate denominator spread to the fixed reciprocal sum through mean inequalities.
why: Quantitative spread bounds can distinguish balanced and highly skewed certificate families.
first_step: Derive the sharp lower bound on x+y+z over positive real solutions and inspect the integer gap for small p.

title: Stationary points of certificate cost
connection: Minimize smooth proxies such as log(xyz) on the real ES surface under specified denominator ordering and bounds.
why: Critical points indicate where an integer search should concentrate, not where integer solutions must exist.
first_step: Use Lagrange multipliers for one bounded cost and compare its minimizers with actual small certificates.

title: Curvature-adapted sampling
connection: Sample near the real solution surface with density adjusted to local curvature and rounding sensitivity.
why: This may propose integer candidates more efficiently than sampling a rectangular box.
first_step: Compute the Hessian of z=pxy/(4xy−p(x+y)) and compare two bounded sampling schemes.

title: Transport between neighboring prime surfaces
connection: Map real points on the p surface to nearby points on the p′ surface and measure the exact integer rounding defect.
why: The defect may suggest a correction identity linking nearby instances.
first_step: Scale a known triple by p′/p, round two coordinates, and factor the exact residual for the third.

title: Optimal transport of divisor-residue measures
connection: Compare residue distributions from two auxiliary parameters using a cost based on allowed residue moves.
why: A low-cost transport plan might identify concrete transformations connecting complementary families.
first_step: For a small modulus, solve a finite transport problem between two divisor-residue histograms and inspect its dominant edges.

title: Finite Fourier uncertainty
connection: Relate concentration of a divisor-residue distribution to concentration of its Fourier transform.
why: A distribution supported on too few residues must carry detectable spectral structure in a finite group.
first_step: Compute support and Fourier support for exact small examples and identify the characters responsible for concentration.

title: Harmonic analysis beyond the unit group
connection: Use the full multiplicative residue monoid when auxiliary factors are not units, rather than forcing a group model.
why: A monoid representation can retain valuation strata that ordinary character expansions omit.
first_step: Construct multiplication operators on residues modulo 12 and decompose their invariant subspaces.

title: SAT encodings of bounded denominator search
connection: Encode the cleared ES equation and positivity bounds as a Boolean circuit with explicit carries.
why: A satisfying assignment is an exactly checkable finite witness, and the encoding may expose reusable logical constraints.
first_step: Build a tiny bounded instance for p=13 and compare decoded models with direct enumeration.

title: SMT over mixed integer structures
connection: Combine integer arithmetic, divisibility, and bit-vector residue constraints in a bounded solver model.
why: Different theories may cooperate better than one large expanded polynomial equation.
first_step: Model one auxiliary divisor family with explicit finite bounds and compare integer-only with mixed-theory formulations.

title: Quantifier elimination for fixed ansatzes
connection: Use real or Presburger quantifier elimination only on subproblems whose language genuinely fits those methods.
why: Exact parameter-region descriptions could simplify one family without pretending general nonlinear integer arithmetic is decidable.
first_step: Choose a linear-congruence ansatz and eliminate one bounded parameter using a Presburger tool.

title: Counterexample-guided identity synthesis
connection: Alternate proposing symbolic denominator formulas with finding primes or parameter values violating their claimed domain.
why: Counterexamples refine the synthesis grammar while every accepted identity requires symbolic verification.
first_step: Run a small CEGIS loop over affine numerator and denominator templates restricted to one residue class.

title: Syntax-guided parametrizations
connection: Define a grammar of gcd, floor, product, and reciprocal operations and search short candidate certificate programs.
why: A restricted grammar makes discovery auditable and encourages explicit formulas rather than opaque predictions.
first_step: Enumerate expressions of depth at most three and test exact identities on a training set before symbolic checking.

title: Equality saturation for rational identities
connection: Store equivalent rational expressions in an e-graph and extract forms with simpler integrality conditions.
why: Equivalent formulas can have very different arithmetic usability even when their real values agree.
first_step: Build an e-graph from a few verified reciprocal identities and score expressions by denominator-factor complexity.

title: Abstract interpretation of parameters
connection: Propagate intervals, congruence classes, and sign information through a candidate denominator program.
why: A sound abstract domain can prove that many inputs produce positive integers without enumerating them.
first_step: Implement transfer rules for addition, multiplication, and exact division on interval-congruence pairs.

title: Constraint propagation on factor domains
connection: Maintain finite domains for factor residues and remove choices that cannot participate in a valid complementary pair.
why: Arc consistency can sharply reduce bounded search while preserving every actual solution.
first_step: Apply AC-3 to a three-variable factor-residue model and compare remaining domains with exhaustive solutions.

title: Modular conflict learning
connection: When a parameter box fails for a provable modular reason, store that reason as a reusable nogood.
why: Learned conflicts can apply across many primes sharing the same local labels.
first_step: Extract one sound modular conflict clause from a failed bounded search and test its reuse on other instances.

title: Proof complexity of bounded failures
connection: Compare lengths of machine-checkable unsatisfiability proofs for different bounded ES encodings.
why: Short proofs may reveal elementary exclusions worth expressing as human lemmas.
first_step: For several deliberately too-small boxes, compare proof sizes under direct and factorized encodings.

title: Proof-carrying witness search
connection: Make each search result carry the integer arithmetic needed to verify positivity and the cleared identity independently.
why: This decouples experimental algorithms from trust in their implementation.
first_step: Specify a compact witness record and a verifier using only exact integer operations.
